title: Tikkun is in the vessels: a thing and its opposite as one
overview:
Chapter 31 turns to the advantage of the vessels over the lights: there is more *hiskalelus* (inclusion) in the vessels, and that is the main thing of *Tikkun*. A light of *chesed* cannot bear *din*, yet it can shine in a vessel of *gevura*, so the inclusion must come from the vessel. The body shows it (one organ is cured through another, eyes water from onions), and so do thought, speech and action: the further out, the easier it is to smile at someone you would like to kill. In actual deed nothing is pure: water has some fire in it, and even a death sentence, Haman's, takes time to pass through the vessels, and the delay is a *chesed*.

Then a contradiction: the vessel yields to its opposite light because of the inner intention, the Name *MaH* rooted in the *Kav*, as Yael's smile and the salesman's must come from inside. So inclusion is in the inner side of the vessels, while their outside, from the limiting power of the *makif*, does one mission and works miracles in the physical place. That same power divides, and division of labor, as in an army, is what makes *Tikkun*.

sections.title: Tikkun comes from the vessels, because only vessels hold opposites
sections.summary: The vessels have an advantage over the lights: there is more *hiskalelus* (inclusion) in them, and that is the main thing of *Tikkun*. The proof is that the light of *chesed* can shine in a vessel of *gevura*: a light cannot join its opposite, so it must be the vessel.

phrases.he: (לא) והנה יש יתרון מעלה בבחינת הכלים מבחינת האורות, ממה שיש בחינת ההתכללות בכלים יותר מבאורות,
שזהו עיקר בחינת התיקון
phrases.en: That's the main thing of *Tikkun*: it comes *davka* from the *kelim*.

phrases.he: כידוע דעיקר בחינת התיקון הוא בא מריבוי הכלים כו'
phrases.en: The whole thing of *Tikkun* is *ribui hakelim*.

phrases.he: ודוקא על ידי בחינת חיצוניות הכלי, שהוא בחינת נה''י כו'

blocks.text: The vessels have an advantage over the lights: there is more *hiskalelus* (inclusion, one thing included in another) in the *kelim* (vessels) than in the *oros* (lights), and that is the main thing of *Tikkun* (the world of Repair). *Tikkun* comes *davka* (precisely) from the vessels, from *ribui hakelim*, the many vessels, and *davka* through the outside of the vessel, *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*). He points to what is in front of them: the *Tikkun* of the explanation is that there are so many explanations, *davka* in the external letters.

phrases.he: וראיה לזה ממה שמצינו בכמה מקומות דאור החסד יוכל להאיר בכלי הגבורה ואור הגבורה בכלי החסד ואם כן, מה שיחליף האור להאיר בכלי היפוכו,
אם היה זה מצד עצמו למה לא יוכלל ויחובר באור היפוכו המנגדו?
phrases.en: If it was from the side of the light, why can't the light get conjoined with another light?

phrases.he: כמו אור מדת החסד שלא יסבול אור מדת הדין כלל וכלל
אלא מוכרח לומר שזהו מצד בחינת הכלי, שיכול לסבול אור היפוכה המנגדה
phrases.en: It's *davka* the *kli* that can take opposite light.

phrases.he: כי יש בכלים דוקא בחינת וענין ההתכללות מדבר והיפוכו, מה שאין כן באורות כו'

blocks.text: As the proof is read, a listener remarks that by this measure the "New and Improved Kabbalah Series" is lights of *Tohu* (chaos) in vessels of *Tikkun*: when the Rebbe spoke of them, he meant, write it. It is this *Shaar HaYichud* (the Gate of Unity). That's exactly it, he agrees: the key of *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) is to give the light many vessels, *davka* the outside of the vessel, explanations that reach the total external world. That is the *Tikkun*.

The proof: in many places the light of *chesed* (kindness) shines in the vessel of *gevura* (might, restraint), and the light of *gevura* in the vessel of *chesed*. If the light changed over from its own side, why could it not be joined with the opposite light itself? **If it was from the side of the light, why can't the light get conjoined with another light?** The light of *chesed* cannot bear the light of *din* (judgement) at all. So **it's *davka* the *kli* that can take opposite light**: vessels hold a thing and its opposite, lights do not.

sections.title: The body: one organ can heal another, through the vessels
sections.summary: *Tikkun* in a person is mainly from the side of his body. One organ can be cured by treating another, because the vessels are included in one another; but a weakness in the light itself, like failing sight from old age, is not cured by strengthening the light of the heart.

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר התיקון בבחינת האדם מצד גופו
phrases.en: The main *Tikkun* in a way of an *adam* is not so much from the side of the soul, but *davka* from the side of the body.

phrases.he: כמו שאנו רואים בחוש טבעי אברי האדם, שכל אחד יש בו התכללות מזולתו,
עד שיכולים להשלים חסרון א' על ידי רפואת אבר זולתו
phrases.en: You can fix one up from fixing up another one.

phrases.he: כמו לקלקול הראות בעין ירפאו לכח הגידין שברגל, שיש בהן בהתכללות מגידין שבעין

blocks.text: The main *Tikkun* of a person is not so much from the side of the soul as *davka* from the side of the body. Each organ has something of the others included in it, so you can fix one by fixing another: the sight of the eye is treated through the nerves of the foot. He's talking about acupuncture: "See, they knew about acupuncture back then."

phrases.he: אבל לא ירפאו לאור וחיות שנחלש במוח עד שנחלש בראות מצד הזקנה וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: When the *chalishus* is from the inside, not from the *kelim*, then you can't do that.

phrases.he: על ידי חיזוק כח ואור חיות המדות שבלב,
phrases.en: Where the light of the mind is starting to go, you can't just work up some heavy *middos* and it'll help it; it won't.

phrases.he: אף על פי שהמוח ולב כלולים זה עם זה
רק מצד חיזוק כלי הלב יחזקו לכלי המוח
phrases.en: But the strengthening of the heart will actually help the brain also.

phrases.he: ויאיר כח השכל בראות יותר כו' מפני שאין לאור השכל עם אור המדות חיבור והתכללות כל כך, כמו שיש חיבור והתכללות של כלי הלב עם כלי המוח וכן כלי העין עם כלי החוטם וכלי האוזן וכהאי גוונא ולזה הטעם הנה דוקא מצד בחינת הכלי יוכל להאיר בה אור המנגדה כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: Not so when the weakness is from the inside, not from the vessels: when the light and life of the brain grow weak, until the sight weakens from old age. Where the light of the mind is starting to go, you can't just work up some heavy *middos* (emotional attributes) in the heart and expect it to help the mind, though brain and heart are included in each other. It won't. But strengthening the vessel of the heart does help the vessel of the brain.

blocks.title: Exercise, and a shot for the brain
blocks.text: Exercise helps everything, the brain included. And if somebody has an infection in his brain, you can give him a shot in his *tachas* (behind); you don't have to put it straight into his brain.

sensitivity.reason: A coarse word for where the shot is given, in a medical example a reader could take as advice.
sensitivity.publishable: Exercise helps everything, the brain included. And if somebody has an infection in his brain, the treatment can be given elsewhere in the body; it doesn't have to go straight into his brain.

blocks.text: For the light of the intellect and the light of the *middos* are not so joined and included in each other as the vessel of the heart is with the vessel of the brain. So too the vessel of the eye with the vessel of the nose: that's why your eyes start to water when you smell onions. Or the ear. For this reason, *davka* through the vessel the opposing light can shine.

sections.title: Chesed and gevura in thought, speech and action: a person can act against his heart
sections.summary: *Chesed* and *gevura* are the most opposite of the *middos*. Yet once they come into the vessels of thought, speech and action, a person can smile at the one he hates, and the further out the vessel, the easier: all because vessels hold a thing and its opposite.

phrases.he: ויובן זה יותר במה שאנו רואים במדות חסד וגבורה
שהן הפכיים מנגדיים ממש כו'
phrases.en: From all the different *middos*, *chesed* and *gevura* are the most opposite ones.

blocks.text: Of all the *middos*, *chesed* and *gevura* are the most opposite. *Chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding) have opposite *tnuos* (movements), but they are not opposite things; really they do the same thing. *Netzach* and *hod* too are opposite movements, not opposite things. *Chesed* and *gevura* are *mamash* (actually) opposite: they go against each other, each doing exactly the opposite of the other.

phrases.he: אך כאשר באין המדות בכלי, כמו למחשבה ולדבור ומעשה בפועל ממש,
phrases.en: When it comes in *kelim*, in other words, of *machshava*, *dibur* and *maaseh* in actuality,

phrases.he: יוכל אור החסד להאיר במחשבה ודבור ומעשה היפוכו ממש שהרי יכול לחשוב ולדבר ולעשות נגד מה שבלבו

blocks.text: But **when it comes in *kelim*, in other words, of *machshava*, *dibur* and *maaseh* in actuality** (thought, speech and action), the light of *chesed* can shine in thought, speech and action that are its very opposite. A person can think, speak and do against what is in his heart.

blocks.title: Yael's smile and the car salesman
blocks.text: Like the women he spoke of before, Yehudis and Yael: they gave him a big smile, and that's the whole thing. Or the car salesman, who smiles at you like he loves you. A person can act against his heart, and the further out you go, the easier it is: to think the opposite is not so easy, to talk it is easier, and to act opposite to what's inside your heart is very easy.

phrases.he: וגם לכעוס בלב על אוהבו בלבו, ולרחם בלבו על שונאו כו' שהלב מוכן להיות כלי למה שהוא היפוכו כו', לפי שבכלים יש התכללות דבר והיפוכו יותר מבאורות
(דמה שבגילה יש רעדה וברוגז יש רחמים, וכן להיפך, ברעדה גילה וברחמים רוגז,
phrases.en: In happiness, there is also fear, and in anger, there's also mercy, and vice versa.

phrases.he: הכל מצד הכלי דוקא כו')
phrases.en: This is all *davka* from the *kelim*.

blocks.text: Even anger in the heart at the one he loves, and mercy on his enemy, is possible, because the heart is a vessel; but in the heart it is not so easy. *Adraba* (just the opposite), the more external, the easier. So **in happiness, there is also fear, and in anger, there's also mercy, and vice versa**. **This is all *davka* from the *kelim***: in the light of happiness itself there is no fear.

sections.title: In the deed there is no pure din: the six days, the verdict, and the death sentence
sections.summary: Each of the six days has its own work, yet every day includes the others, because a day is a vessel. Whatever comes into actual deed is composite: even a sentence of death is held up by the vessels it must pass through, and the delay is already *chesed*.

phrases.he: וכך אנו מוצאים בששת ימי המעשה,
phrases.en: This we find in the six days,

phrases.he: שביום א' הוא בחינת חסד - יהי אור, וביום הב' בחינת גבורה - יהי רקיע כו',
וכמו שכתוב בזהר דכל יומא בעבידתיה כו'
phrases.en: Every day has its own special work.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה בכל יום יש התכללות מיום זולתו דוקא כידוע
phrases.en: But nonetheless, you see that in every day, there's really the *inyan* of all days.

phrases.he: לפי שכאשר בא האור בכלי שנקרא יום, אז יש התכללות דבר והיפוכו דוקא

blocks.text: So with the six days of creation, which are vessels. The first day is *chesed*, "Let there be light"; the second is *gevura*, "Let there be a firmament", to separate; as the *Zohar* says, **every day has its own special work**. **But nonetheless, you see that in every day, there's really the *inyan* of all days**: in Sunday and Monday of the week, really all the *inyanim* are there. For when the light comes into the vessel called a day, there is a thing and its opposite.

phrases.he: להיות שכאשר בא הדבר לידי השפעה בפועל ממש, אי אפשר שלא יוכלל בחסד מבחינת דין ובדין מבחינת החסד
phrases.en: When a thing is in actuality, then it can't be a perfect; it has to be a *murkav*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשהאור והשפע עדיין בלא כלי כו'

blocks.text: When a thing comes to actual influence, *chesed* cannot be without some *din* in it, nor *din* without *chesed*. **When a thing is in actuality, then it can't be a perfect; it has to be a *murkav*** (composite).

blocks.title: Water always has some fire in it
blocks.text: You can't have water that is just water. Water always has some fire in it, because it has a temperature: even water at room temperature will warm up a colder place, because there is actually fire inside of it. And it is even more *murkav* than that. In the total external there is no such thing as a perfect, non-*murkav* thing.

phrases.he: כמו פסק דין למעשה דוקא שבהכרח יוכלל חסד בדין ודין בחסד
phrases.en: Like a *psak din* for actual *maaseh*: you can't have a totally perfect *din* or *chesed* of a *psak din*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשאינו למעשה כו'
phrases.en: When it's not *lemaaseh*, you can say whatever you want to say.

phrases.he: ונמצא שמצד בחינת חיצוניות הכלי, שהוא למעשה, שם הוא עיקר בחינת ההתכללות כו' ודי למבין:

blocks.text: So with a *psak din* (a verdict) for actual deed: **you can't have a totally perfect *din* or *chesed* of a *psak din***; *chesed* is necessarily included in *din* and *din* in *chesed*. **When it's not *lemaaseh*** (for the deed), **you can say whatever you want to say**. So the outside of the vessel, which is the deed, is where the inclusion mainly is. The easiest way to understand it: in actual deed you can smile opposite to what you feel.

blocks.question: A death sentence: isn't that total gevura?
blocks.text: Not even that. The whole reason in the Torah for the death penalty is to be a *kapara* (atonement) for the person, which is really a *chesed*. And in a regular death penalty, the very fact that there is a trial is already a *chesed*.

blocks.title: We all saw him shoot
blocks.text: We all saw the guy shoot the other guy: what do you mean, a trial? Let's take him and lynch him. But you say: wait a minute, you can't kill him on the spot, you have to have a *beis din* (a court). The *beis din* is a *chesed* for him: it gives him a chance to prove something.

blocks.title: Haman, hanged without a trial
blocks.text: Take the worst case, Haman: no trial. The king got so mad that he said, take him and hang him right now. Still it could not be done at once; it took a while. A listener objects that they took him right out. It doesn't matter: from the *midas hadin* (the attribute of judgement) upstairs he would have died on the spot. Even a gun takes a second, and that time is already a commutation of the *din*.

blocks.question: The only Tikkun for Amalek is to break it. That's perfect din: where's the chesed?
blocks.text: A listener answers that it is a *chesed* after all: his *Tikkun* is to be broken like an earthenware vessel, which once broken is no longer impure. No, that is the next thing the chapter will talk about, the inclusion of the lights: in the source of the light the real thing of *din* is *chesed*, to protect the public. That is in the intention. Even with Amalek, when we're killing him and it's total *din*, the real inner intention of that *din* is *chesed*. But that is in the source of the light, not in the actual deed.

From the side of the vessels it is different: because of the *ribui hakelim*, the many vessels, it takes time, and so there is automatically inclusion. It doesn't just go: as soon as you say he's to die, he's going to die.

From the light, a light of *midas hadin* would not have let there be a world at all. It says that originally He wanted to create the world with *din*, saw that it wouldn't stand, and had to be *meshatef* (join) *chesed* with it. A listener corrects him: it doesn't say *chesed*, it says *rachamim* (mercy). Yes, and *rachamim* means He joins *chesed* with it. So from the side of the light, *din* could not exist *lechatchila* (from the start), and the minute there is a *din* on a man, he would stop existing immediately. In the deed you can't do that.

Say you take a gun out and shoot him: it still takes time, three hours there and three seconds here. He is not dead just because you decided he is dead. It has to go through the vessels, and the vessels hold it up a little: a commutation, a delay of the *din*. And a delay of the *din* is *chesed*.

Not only that: because of the delay there can actually be a change. Nowadays people put on death row can change and go off death row. That was the whole thing with Amalek too: the holding up with Agag *mamash* changed something; he was able to have a continuation. Without the many vessels, the commutation of the sentence, it would be instantaneous, and, as a listener says, the world would be destroyed.

blocks.title: If looks could kill
blocks.text: Achashverosh had a total *din* on Haman, and it still took some time. The minute Haman saw Achashverosh's face, he knew it was all over. Were it from the lights, it would have been all over immediately, like in Harry Potter, where just a look and the guy dies: "if looks could kill". But first they had to say to take him out, and take him, and drag him, and hang him up there. It took time. Because it had to go through the vessels, he got to live longer.

blocks.title: Vashti, had she lived a little longer
blocks.text: And it could even have changed before that, as with Vashti. Had she been kept alive a little longer, Achashverosh would have stopped being mad, and he would have kept her.

In deed, no matter how pure, there is inclusion. Achashverosh's anger was totally pure anger, but because it is actual, it is not totally pure in how it comes out, so the anger can diminish. That's why anger diminishes. In the lights it can't; only because of the vessels does it actually diminish. Your heart gets angry and angrier, but give it a little time and it diminishes. So *davka* in the outside of the vessels is the inclusion.

sections.title: The contradiction: the vessel yields to the opposite light because of the inner intention
sections.summary: Yet what lets a light shine in its opposite vessel is the vessel's *bittul* (yielding) to the light, which comes from within, from the Name *MaH*: the inner intention, rooted in the *Kav*, where *chesed* and *gevura* are one. Yael's smile, the salesman's smile: the smile has to come from the inside of the face. So inclusion is in the inner side of the vessels, not in the deed itself, and an angel can carry only one mission.

phrases.he: אך הנה לכאורה יש סתירה לכל זה שהרי באמת, מה שהאור יוכל להאיר בכלי היפוכו, הוא מצד בחינת הביטול של הכלי לגבי האור
והוא על ידי בחינת שם מ''ה מלגאו,
phrases.en: It's really from the inner intention, from the inside.

phrases.he: שרש בחינת ההתכללות באורות,
דוקא מצד הארת הקו כו'
phrases.en: And that comes from the *haaras hakav*.

blocks.text: But at first glance there is a contradiction to all this. What lets the light shine in its opposite vessel is really the *bittul* (self-nullification) of the vessel to the light, and that comes through the Name *MaH* (of forty-five; he reads "of *Adam Kadmon*", the first world): **it's really from the inner intention, from the inside**.

blocks.title: Yael's smile
blocks.text: Yael was able to smile at Sisera really because of the inner intention, the Name *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon*. The inner intention of what the *midda* is going to be changed it over, so that the vessel became *batel* (nullified) to the light. That's why she was able to do it.

blocks.title: The salesman's smile
blocks.text: How come the salesman can smile at you like that? Because of the inner intention: he wants to make money. A listener offers the *goyishe* (non-Jewish) saying, "Don't get angry, get even." Yes, but the *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon* here is his self-image, of being the greatest salesman. That's why he can smile at you; so too when you go to Disneyland.

blocks.question: What does self-image have to do with Yael?
blocks.text: Her self-image, her *Adam Kadmon*, was that she intended to kill him and was willing to do anything to accomplish it. That was in the intention, her original inner intention, not in the vessel.

blocks.title: Mata Hari
blocks.text: She saw herself as a Mata Hari, ready to go to total *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) to do what needed to be done. She wanted to kill him so much that she was even willing to look as if she was not angry and treat him nicely. And she had to really treat him nicely, or he would feel it: an act put on with actual *middos*, not just with vessels. That is what made the vessels *batel* to the light: it came from the inner *MaH*.

The inner *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon* said this is how it should be. From the light itself the intention might not be like that, but the inner-inner intention was. Especially since *Adam Kadmon* is a *ratzon l'ratzon* (a will for a will): a will to come up with any will you need to get the thing done.

blocks.title: I never met a man I didn't like
blocks.text: A man whose *Adam Kadmon* is being a great salesman has a will to have a will to like anybody, as Will Rogers said, "I never met a man I didn't like." But the real intention is not necessarily to do him good. It is a will to find a good way to talk to him.

You see this in missionaries, who are a kind of salesmen. They work themselves up to love everybody, and really love them, but it is not really a love: it is an intention of hate. It is really an intention of *gevura*, which is control. They want to control this person.

sensitivity.reason: Says missionaries' love for the people they approach is really an intention of hate and control.

blocks.text: So too *How to Win Friends and Influence People*: look at it, and the title of the book is to control people. It's a great-selling book.
So it is the intent of the intent, the *ratzon l'ratzon*, and the Name *MaH*, which is even before the *ratzon l'ratzon*: the actual intent of what he wants to do.

The root of the inclusion in the lights is *davka* the *haaras hakav* (the shining of the *Kav*, the line of light). In the *Kav* all the lights are really the same, because the *Kav* is the essence of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite), and in the *Ein Sof* *chesed* and *gevura* are *mamash* the same thing. The inner intent of *gevura* is *chesed*, and the inner intent of the king's *chesed* is to have proper courts of law.

blocks.question: Why are they called chasidei umos haolam (the kindly of the nations), when the whole matter of the seven mitzvos, a court of law included, is davka din?
blocks.text: Because from this *din* comes a world of *chesed*. *Davka* from *din* comes a world of *chesed*, not from a world of *chesed*; from a world of *chesed*, if you just let anybody do whatever he wants, would actually come a world of *din*. It seems just opposite.

So the inclusion really comes from the lights, and the *bittul* is *davka* in the *pnimiyus hakelim* (the inner side of the vessels), where the light hits and the vessel feels the inner intention and yields to it. A salesman's real smile has to come from the inside of his face, or it looks phony. He has to convince himself he really feels it: the light must be a light of a smile, though the intention is only control, which is *gevura*.

phrases.he: ולזה הטעם, דוקא בפנימיות הכלים יש התכללות
(וכמו הכונה שבמעשה המצות שמתכלל ב' הפכים כו'
phrases.en: Like the *kavana* in the *maaseh* of the *mitzvos* that brings together two *hafachim*,

phrases.he: והיינו כמו עצמות וגידים כו'
phrases.en: and that's like the bones and the nerves that come out of them,

phrases.he: מה שאין כן גוף המעשה)
phrases.en: where in the *guf hamaaseh* it's not like that.

phrases.he: ולא בחיצוניות
שהרי אין מלאך א' עושה ב' שליחות הפכים
phrases.en: A *malach* can't do two *shlichuses*.

phrases.he: מפני שכל שליחות השפע בא מחיצוניות הכלים דוקא,
שמביא השפע לחוץ
phrases.en: that brings the *hashpaa* of it to the outside.

phrases.he: כמו חיצוניות הכלי דאותיות וכהאי גוונא
ולכך פני אריה להימין כו',
phrases.en: By the angels, you see the lion is on the right, and the ox is on the left, always.

phrases.he: לא ישנו את תפקידם
phrases.en: And they can't change.

phrases.he: ולא יתחברו להחליף מעשיהם מזה לזה כו'
phrases.en: And they won't join together to change over.

phrases.he: ולכך כל יומא בעבידתיה דווקא כו'.
phrases.en: That's why each day has its own work.

blocks.text: For this reason the inclusion is *davka* in the inner side of the vessels: **like the *kavana* in the *maaseh* of the *mitzvos* that brings together two *hafachim*** (the intention in doing the *mitzvos*, which joins two opposites), **and that's like the bones and the nerves that come out of them**, **where in the *guf hamaaseh*** (the body of the deed) **it's not like that**. In the deed itself there is no inclusion.
The next tape picks up: the inclusion is *davka* in the inner side, the *kavanos* of the deed, and in the *kavanos* two different intentions can go together. The body of the deed is only one thing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 047 opens by finishing class 046's reading of line 35, before it reads line 36 (w46).

blocks.text: For one angel does not do two opposite missions. Even if the outer vessel is doing *din* while the inner light is *chesed*, the vessel is doing *din*, and that's all it's doing; it can't do *din* and *chesed* at the same time. Only in a light can two opposite intentions work together. A smile is not a frown. **A *malach* can't do two *shlichuses*** (missions). Either he's an angel of a smile or an angel of a frown; even if inside him is a frown, as an angel he does one mission.

Why? Because every mission of influence comes *davka* from the outside of the vessel, **that brings the *hashpaa* of it to the outside** (the influence), and to bring it out you can only bring it out one way, not two. It makes no difference what you say: the outside of the vessel is what it is. Only the inside of the vessel is *batel* to the opposite thing.

So with the outer vessel of letters. **By the angels, you see the lion is on the right, and the ox is on the left, always**, **and they can't change**, nor take turns. A *patsch* (a slap) is a *patsch* and a smile is a smile: whether a *patsch* of *chesed* or of *gevura*, the *patsch* itself is a vessel of *gevura* only. **That's why each day has its own work.**

sections.title: Two sources: the inner light in the vessel, and the limiting power of the makif
sections.summary: The inner side of the vessel receives the inner light, so when the lights are included in one another so is the inside of the vessel, as in the feelings of Michael and Gavriel. The outside of the vessel comes from the limiting power of the *makif*, which bears two opposites at once: hence miracles happen in the physical place itself.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא משום דפנימית הכלי הוא מקבל מבחינת אור פנימי המוגבל בכלי,
וכאשר יש התכללות באורות, ממילא יש התכללות בפנימית הכלים,
phrases.en: When there's *hiskalelus* in the *oros*, then there can be *hiskalelus* *bepnimiyus hakelim*.

phrases.he: כמו התפעלות והשגות מיכאל וגבריאל כו'
phrases.en: Like in the *hispaalus* and *hasagos* of Michael and Gavriel.

phrases.he: וחיצוניות הכלים מבחינת הכח המגביל שבבחינת מקיף
phrases.en: The *chitzoniyus hakelim* comes from the actual *koach hamegbil*, which is in a way of a *makif*.

blocks.text: The matter is this. The inner side of the vessel receives from the inner light limited in the vessel. **When there's *hiskalelus* in the *oros*** (which comes from the *Kav*, from the inner *kavana* that receives the light), **then there can be *hiskalelus* *bepnimiyus hakelim***: **like in the *hispaalus* and *hasagos* of Michael and Gavriel**, their excitement and grasp, which is their inner side, not their actions. And **the *chitzoniyus hakelim*** (the outside of the vessels) **comes from the actual *koach hamegbil*** (the power that limits), **which is in a way of a *makif*** (the encompassing light).

phrases.he: על כן יש בו ב' הפכים כאחד, בחינת התכללות דבר והיפוכו דוקא
phrases.en: Therefore *davka* over there you can really have a thing and its opposite.

phrases.he: כמו כל הנסים, שהם דוקא בבחינת חיצוניות הכלים בפועל ממש
phrases.en: The whole thing of a *nes* is *davka* in the *chitzoniyus hakelim*.

phrases.he: כמו כל מקום שנעשה בו הנס, שהמקום הזה סובל דבר והיפוכו, מלמעלה מן הטבע בטבע כו'
phrases.en: The actual place can take a thing and its opposite, higher than the *teva* inside the *teva*.

phrases.he: כהפיכת ים ליבשה כו',
phrases.en: Like to change over the ocean to dry land.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא מקום הארון אינו מן המדה וכו', וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר

blocks.text: So the outside holds two opposites as one: **therefore *davka* over there you can really have a thing and its opposite**. However Yael did it, she killed him: the deed had the opposite effect outside, literally, and did a mission opposite to itself.

blocks.question: How does "two opposites at once" follow from the limiting power of the makif?
blocks.text: Because the *makif* is not like the inner light, where it is either this or that. It is not an actual *gvul* (limit) but a *koach hamegbil*, a power to limit. Of the *makif* it says one does not know the difference between Haman and Mordechai, Esav and Yaakov: *davka* there you can have a thing and its opposite.

So every *nes* (miracle) is *davka* in the actual outside of the vessels: the water stood up. The place where the miracle happened bears a thing and its opposite, above nature inside nature: **like to change over the ocean to dry land**, a miracle done not in a spiritual fashion but *davka* in a physical one. So too the place of the Ark took up no space: we are talking about the actual Ark and the actual measurement.

blocks.question: Is that the same thing as the mother who, in a sudden panic, can lift a car?
blocks.text: Yes: that is from the power of the *makif*, which does not come through a *tzimtzum* (contraction); it comes directly.

sections.title: Division of labor: the division that makes Tikkun
sections.summary: From the *makif*'s line of measure also comes the root of *hischalkus*, each vessel separate by itself. That is the main thing of *Tikkun*: the division of labor, as in an army, makes a unity greater than any single warrior, even where all share one will.

phrases.he: וגם משם הוא בא שרש בחינת ההתחלקות, כל אחד מובדל בפני עצמו
phrases.en: And also from there comes the *shoresh* of the *hischalkus*, that each one is *muvdal* by itself.

phrases.he: שהוא בא מצד בחינת קו המדה שבמקיף, שהוא שרש הכלים המגבילים כו'

blocks.text: **And also from there comes the *shoresh* of the *hischalkus*, that each one is *muvdal* by itself** (the root of division, each one separate): each vessel is *davka* its own thing. From the beginning of the line, the *makif*, come both: the inclusion where they are all the same, and the division. That is the *kav hamida* (the line of measure) in the *makif*. As said before, it has two *inyanim*: it connects everything and holds all the opposites, and it separates everything, this is *chesed* and this is *gevura*. It is the root of the limiting vessels.

phrases.he: ולזה עיקר בחינת התיקון הוא בחינת ריבוי ההתחלקות דוקא
phrases.en: That's why it's *davka* from the divisions that come the unification.

blocks.text: So the main thing of *Tikkun* is many divisions: **that's why it's *davka* from the divisions that come the unification**. As said, the power that divides is the power that unites.

blocks.title: Division of labor: the army
blocks.text: The whole thing of *Tikkun* is basically what is called division of labor. It is *davka* the division of labor that makes an army: each one divided into his own job, and so when they are all together there is the inclusion of a greater thing than if each guy did everything. If each guy did everything, nobody would be a great driller.

blocks.title: A cluster of computers
blocks.text: A listener adds the computer cluster: they divide the work over a whole bunch of processors, and a thousand computers are better than one supercomputer that can only do one thing at a time. It's *davka* the division that gives the inclusion.

That is the army. The army is a whole thing of inclusion, and what gives it the inclusion is the division, which is *davka* in the outside of the vessels: this guy is army and that guy navy, this one a gunner and that one a flyer. That is what makes the *Tikkun* of the army.

blocks.title: The cook and the dishwasher
blocks.text: It may look as if the inclusion comes from the inside, from the inner intention joining the various intentions; really it is not so much from that. *Tikkun* is like an army or a society where each one has his own job. Even in a small business, a restaurant: that guy's the cook and that guy cleans the dishes. Where everybody does everything, it doesn't work so good, and there is no inclusion.
Not only that: too many cooks spoil the broth, like what happened with the Alter Rebbe, where everybody put salt in.

blocks.question: Why is the vessel batel to the light? It seems to come from the inner side of the vessels.
blocks.text: It seems so: why are they all working together in an army? Not from their outer function; each one is doing his own function. For a common goal, and the common goal is the inner side of the vessel: inside, they're all Americans, which is why they joined the army to begin with. They all have the same light, the same *ratzon* (will). So it looks as if it comes from the inner light hitting the inside of the vessel, not from the outside of the vessels.

Still, the text says, the *Tikkun* of the army comes *davka* from their division into different functions: this one does his own function and not the other. That is how you fly a B-52. It is very nice that they all have the same *ratzon*, but without a fine division it would just be total *Tohu* (chaos), even with the same will.

blocks.title: The Indians and the white man's army
blocks.text: That is why the white man conquered the Indian. From the side of the light, their inner side, the Indians were more unified and more heroic. But each one was a whole brave, each one an army. You couldn't tell him: you can't have the glory, you'll be the guy who cleans the fish. "What do you mean? I'm a brave. I want to earn my feathers." In the white man's army some soldiers couldn't care less; they were career soldiers, not so brave. But they were separated into different functions. The Indians each wanted all the glory and would go whooping into battle.

sensitivity.reason: Pictures Native Americans as glory-seeking braves who "go whooping into battle".
sensitivity.publishable: That is why the white man conquered the Indian. From the side of the light, their inner side, the Indians were more unified and more heroic. But each one was a whole brave, each one an army. You couldn't tell him: you can't have the glory, you'll be the guy who cleans the fish. "What do you mean? I'm a brave. I want to earn my feathers." In the white man's army some soldiers couldn't care less; they were career soldiers, not so brave. But they were separated into different functions. The Indians each wanted all the glory.

phrases.he: שבזה דוקא יהיה ריבוי ההתכללות,
דבר והיפוכו כאחד
phrases.en: A thing and its opposite like one.

blocks.text: So it's *davka* the division of labor that makes the *Tikkun*: only with division can there be a joining into a higher grouping, like the white army. The Indians had no division of labor, though from the inside they were more unified, standing on principle and defending their own land; the same with the Romans. With each one doing his specialty, an army can conquer a bunch of guys each of whom is a whole army by himself.

By the Indians there could be no inclusion: with no division, each one did the same whole thing by himself, so inclusion of what? **A thing and its opposite like one**: one man does the hero's thing while another is a milquetoast in the office writing reports, a pencil pusher, the very opposite of a soldier. Try to get an Indian to be a pencil pusher: "What, I'm going to sit and push a pencil? I want the glory. I'm a warrior."

sensitivity.reason: Continues the picture of the Indian as a glory-seeking warrior who would scorn a desk job.
sensitivity.publishable: By the Indians there could be no inclusion: with no division, each one did the same whole thing by himself, so inclusion of what? **A thing and its opposite like one**: one man does the hero's thing while another is a milquetoast in the office writing reports, a pencil pusher, the very opposite of a soldier. Try to get a born warrior to be a pencil pusher: he wants the glory.

sections.title: Adam of Tikkun: "behind and before You formed me"
sections.summary: The main thing of *Adam* of *Tikkun* is the division of organs. The matter comes both before the light, as its root and the vision of the end, and after it, in the physical body: the whole matter of the chain of descent, *yesh* from *yesh*.

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר בחינת אדם דתיקון כו',
phrases.en: The main thing of *Adam* is that there's a division of organs.

phrases.he: שעליו אמר אחור וקדם צרתני, יצירה בגוף חומר דוקא כו' קדם, בבחינת החומר הפשוט שקדם לצורה, שהוא האור והוא בשרש הכלי שקדם לאור
ואחור, בכלי החומר שאחר האור והצורה כו'
phrases.en: That comes after the light, and it's through the actual physical thing.

phrases.he: ודי למבין וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר ביאור ענין זה באריכות (ודי למבין):

blocks.text: This is the main thing of *Adam* of *Tikkun*: **the main thing of *Adam* is that there's a division of organs**. Of him it says "behind and before You formed me". "Before": the simple matter that precedes the form, which is the light; the final matter of the actual body preceded the light, as the vision of the final thing, of how the whole army will be moving together. It is in the root of the vessel, which precedes the light.

"And behind": the matter precedes the light, and it is also after the light, in the vessel of matter **that comes after the light, and it's through the actual physical thing**. This, by the way, is the whole matter of the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) *yesh m'yesh* (something from something): the true *yesh*, the final person, comes from the actual thing that preceded the light altogether.

reviewQuestions.question: How does the light of chesed shining in a vessel of gevura prove that inclusion comes from the vessels and not from the lights?
Why can one organ be cured by treating another, while failing sight from old age is not cured by strengthening the middos of the heart?
Why is it easier to act against your heart than to think against it, and what do Yael and the car salesman show?
In what way is even a death sentence, Haman's for example, not pure din once it comes to the deed?
If the vessel yields to its opposite light because of the inner intention, why can one angel still do only one mission?
How does the division of labor in an army make it more united than warriors who share one will?
